name: Phoenix
what: The upkeep cycle: registered checks that repair themselves from a declared fix or say so out loud. One clock per LAN - a node's Phoenix reflects the root's beat instead of running a second schedule, so this box publishes node.<ref>.build and (as a child) no beat of its own; a SKEW against the root's build is the only version fault there is. The instance with PHOENIX_STATE set is the root: it publishes lan.cycle and writes every node's beat from the same clock.
note: This file used to read {module, door, title}. The shelf reads {name, port, start, wiredAtBoot}, so on every node Phoenix was listed with port null and start null: installed, never wired, never started, and therefore invisible to the fleet version check. That is why five boxes reported no build while their owner knew the module was there.
